classes_note: Four classes, each the census's own kind, text object, evidence kind, finding or worked question for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) the Dead Sea Scrolls, the corpus the library images (census text_object, coverage; B1, B5, B7, B8); (2) Second Temple Jewish religious literature, the non-biblical scrolls with apocalyptic texts among them (B7; census text_object); (3) the dating of the scrolls (census findings[1], answers[1], relation used_by enoch-dss-dating; B7, B8); (4) digitized manuscript images and online digital libraries (census kind, evidence_kind 'manuscript images', worked question 'seen-or-edited'; B1, B3, B5, B8). The census's intersections for the entity are 'papyrology-discovery' and 'nt-scholarship'; its negative tags are 'NOT a New Testament collection' and 'NOT an edition: images and introductions'. The archive bears on these classes through the Revelation First thesis (#202 and the deposits revelationfirst.com cites), its papyrological work and its machine-reading work; a deposit enters only where its sentence says something of the entity or applies its category to one of these classes. The census's rf_intersection ('Context and method: the Second Temple literature behind the Apocalypse's imagery, and the corpus on which the Enoch model moved palaeographic dates earlier against radiocarbon anchors') is the archive's reading, ledgered as RF-; it does not by itself admit a deposit. Aliases: the full name, the name without 'Leon Levy', the site's host and the short form 'Leon Levy Library' (B3). The bare 'Leon Levy' is not an alias: it is the financier and the Leon Levy Foundation, whose other works (the Shelby White & Leon Levy Lod Mosaic Center, B5's navigation) are distinct.
